https://telex.hu/gazdasag/2026/08/17/4ig.text: Menü Kereső Durván bezuhant a 4iG, miután Magyar Péter a szájára vette a céget Gazdaság Csurgó Dénes Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Több mint 12 százalékot zuhant hétfő délutánra a 4iG részvényárfolyama, miután Magyar Péter hosszan sorolta egy Facebook-videóban azt, milyen üzleteket, szerződéseket akar megvizsgálni a kormány. A részvény már reggel is 5 százalékos eséssel kezdte a napot hétfőn a Portfolio.hu cikke szerint a korai árfolyamesés valószínűleg azt jelentette hogy a befektetők most reagáltak a péntek esti bejelentés hírére, miszerint a kormány átfogó vizsgálatot rendelt el a 4iG-csoport és a magyar állam közötti kapcsolatról . A bejelentés óta erre most volt először alkalmuk, mert hétvégén nincs nyitva a tőzsde. Hétfő kora délután a Jászai Gellért vezette IT, a távközlés, a hadiipar és az űripar területén is dolgozó, a magyar állammal mindegyik piacon nagyon szoros kapcsolatban lévő cég részvényárfolyama már csak 3,9 százalékponttal volt a pénteki záróárfolyam alatt, vagyis valamennyit erősödött a tőzsdenyitás utáni esést követően. Amint a grafikonon látható, az árfolyam a múlt hét második felében erősödött, hogy aztán onnan essen vissza a hétvége után. Délután 3 körül aztán Magyar Péter közzétett egy több mint 7 perces videót a Facebook-oldalán, ahol a 4iG és az Orbán-kormány összefonódásairól, az Antenna Hungária privatizálásától és visszaállamosításától a Vodafone Magyarország megvásárlásán át a hadiipari cégek részleges privatizálásáig, a Gondosóra-programig és a 4iG-vel a választások előtt megkötött milliárdos szerződésekig. Magyar Péter a videóban a NER egyik lopakodó anyahajójának nevezte a 4iG-t, amihez stratégiai fontosságú vagyonelemek kerültek az Orbán-kormány alatt közpénz százmilliárdok felhasználásával, és amelynek minden szerződését át fogják vizsgálni, beleértve a hadiipari cégvásárlásokat, az Antenna Hungária körüli bizniszt és a Vodafone megvásárlásának finanszírozását is. Magyar videója után az addig stabilizálódó árfolyam ismét zuhanni kezdett, fél 5-re már több mint 12 százalékkal volt a pénteki záróárfolyam alatt. A péntek este, tőzsdezárás után megjelent Magyar Közlönyben az szerepel, hogy Kapitány István gazdasági és energetikai miniszter, Ruszin-Szendi Romulusz honvédelmi miniszter, Kármán András pénzügyminiszter és Tanács Zoltán tudományos és technológiai miniszter fognak nyilvános tájékoztatást adni a vizsgálatok lezárulta után. A vizsgálatról, valamint a 4iG és az Orbán-kormány összefonódásairól hétfőn Magyar Péter is beszélt Facebook-oldalán . A 4iG részvényárfolyama az elmúlt 5 kereskedési napon. – Forrás: TradingView Tanács Zoltán Facebook-oldalán azt írta, a 2015-ös G-nap után, amikor a NER addig prominens oligarchája, Simicska Lajos szakított Orbán Viktorral, ma elérkezett a 4iG-nap.„De van egy nagyon fontos különbség. Most nem egy oligarcha kezdeményezte a szakítást a kormánnyal. Most maga a kormány mondja azt: eddig és ne tovább. És nem a saját érdekében, hanem a nemzet érdekében.” – írja a tudományos és technológiai miniszter. „Szerződéseket, megrendeléseket, konstrukciókat és döntéseket vizsgálunk. Mert a feltárt ügyek számos eleme felveti annak gyanúját, hogy az elmúlt években nem egyszerűen rossz vagy előnytelen szerződések születtek, hanem a magyar állam tudatos megkárosítása is történhetett.” Az, hogy a 4iG-vel kapcsolatban ezeket a minisztereket kérték fel, teljesen logikus, az Orbán-rendszer csúcsvállalatának jövőjét boncolgató korábbi cikkünkben is őket soroltuk fel, mint akik érdekeltek lehetnek a folyamatban. Első ránézésre leginkább az lehet majd érdekes, hogy miért van a Honvédelmi Minisztériumnak egy 10 éves, 1311 milliárd forintos szerződése a tőzsdén jegyzett 4iG-csoporttal, amiről a befektetők, sőt, még egyes vezetők sem tudtak . Ezen felül él egy 2030-ig szóló, 1500 milliárd forintos honvédelmi szerződés is, szóval ezeken a szerződéseken lesz mit nézegetni . Photograph: Raj Valley/Alamy View image in fullscreen No official reason was given for the sacking of Iryna Mudra, a presidential deputy chief of staff. Photograph: Raj Valley/Alamy Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy sacks senior aide amid Ukraine corruption crisis Presidential deputy chief of staff Iryna Mudra dismissed day after former defence minister called for wartime election Dan Sabbagh in Kyiv Wed 19 Aug 2026 13.14 EDT Last modified on Wed 19 Aug 2026 13.50 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy has fired a senior aide amid a fresh corruption investigation – one day after a former defence minister warned the country was facing “a crisis of governance” and needed to hold a wartime presidential election . Iryna Mudra, a presidential deputy chief of staff, was dismissed by decree after multiple reports in Ukrainian media that her house was being searched by officials investigating an alleged money-laundering scheme. Sacking turns former Zelenskyy loyalist into potent political opponent Read more No official reason was given for Mudra’s sacking as Zelenskyy sought to carry on as normal, despite Mykhailo Fedorov’s surprise call for an early presidential election in a video address released late on Tuesday. The president did not directly address the ousted minister’s accusations or his election demand in his initial public statements, though he did thank Ukraine’s parliament for voting to confirm Fedorov’s replacement, Yevhen Khmara, in the post. At the heart of Fedorov’s argument were accusations that corruption remained widespread under Zelenskyy and that the president had failed to get a grip. “Corruption is only a symptom. The main problem runs much deeper. We have a systemic crisis of governance,” Fedorov had said. View image in fullscreen Mykhailo Fedorov has become the first major public figure to call for an election, effectively posing a direct challenge to the sitting president. Photograph: Efrem Lukatsky/AP The removal of Fedorov from his post in July triggered the most significant street protests in Ukraine since the war began. Fedorov is now considering visiting the US, possibly as soon as next week, in an apparent effort to win over American support. In the past, the US president, Donald Trump, has called for Ukraine to hold elections, though his comments were made at a time when his relationship with Zelenskyy was strained. Elections have been suspended in Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022. Fedorov became the first major public figure to call for a presidential poll, effectively posing a direct challenge to the sitting president. “Can Russia effectively be given the right to dictate when Ukrainians can choose their government again? I am convinced that the answer is no,” Fedorov said in a nine-minute video address released on social media late on Tuesday. Zelenskyy’s term notionally expired in spring 2024, but an election during wartime is prohibited by the constitution, and had anyway been considered by most Ukrainians to be impractical and potentially divisive while Russia continues to attack on a daily basis. View image in fullscreen Volodymyr Zelenskyy has not directly addressed Mykhailo Fedorov’s accusations of widespread corruption. Photograph: Oleksandr Magula/Suspilne Ukraine/JSC “UA:PBC”/Global Images Ukraine/Getty Images The Nabu anti-corruption agency said it was conducting a special operation to expose what it said was a criminal conspiracy that involved “the participation of high-ranking officials from the office of the president” and several others. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every day Sign up to Headlines Europe A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day after newsletter promotion It released a video saying those involved included a deputy head of the president’s office, a serving MP and a former MP, as well as the CEO and supervisory board head at a state-owned bank, though none were named. Nabu added that the group was accused of laundering 150m hryvinas (£2.5m) through the state-owned bank in order to post bail in June for the former energy minister Herman Haluschenko, himself facing anti-corruption charges. Haluschenko is a defendant in the high-profile Midas corruption case , alongside the businessman Timur Mindich, who has fled the country. Mindich is a former associate of the president and former co-owner of the TV production company Kvartal 95, co-founded by Zelenskyy in the years before he went into politics. Mindich is accused of orchestrating a large-scale corruption scheme that was uncovered last November in which kickbacks were demanded from companies seeking to supply the country’s state-owned nuclear power generator Energoatom. The scandal damaged Zelenskyy’s credibility. A fortnight later, his then chief aide, Andriy Yermak, resigned after anti-corruption investigators searched his home. He was then arrested in May on suspicion of money laundering. Yermak’s lawyer has dismissed the allegations as “baseless”. Mindich, who fled to Israel, also denies wrongdoing. Later on Wednesday, Zelenskyy presented 25 certificates giving housing to decorated veterans and their families. The president said Ukraine was a country that honoured its heroes and emphasised it was important to be thankful to its bravest troops. “Gratitude is what should accompany respect. It must be an integral part of a normal state, a normal society and normal people,” the president said. It was perhaps the closest he had come all day to making a comment of any kind on the crisis. https://www.globalsecurity.org/wmd/libra.text: Military WMD Menu Introduction Systems Facilities Agencies Operations Countries Hot Documents News Reports Policy Budget Congress Links Intelligence Homeland Security Space Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) Tsahkna: Estonia and Ireland deepen cooperation in supporting Ukraine Republic of Estonia - Ministry of Foreign Affairs 09.09.2026 | 18:25 Today, 9 September, Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna met Ireland's Minister for Foreign Affairs, Defence and Trade Helen McEntee in Tallinn. The meeting focused on increasing support for Ukraine, exerting greater pressure on Russia, including through additional economic sanctions and the use of frozen Russian assets to support Ukraine, and strengthening European security and defence capabilities. The ministers signed a declaration of intent under which Ireland will contribute €1 million to an Estonian-led healthcare and education project in Ukraine. They also discussed Ireland's Presidency of the Council of the European Union and bilateral relations. According to Tsahkna, Ireland, as holder of the EU Presidency, has an important role in advancing Europe's common decisions. "We consider it important to take robust action in supporting Ukraine and exerting pressure on Russia, including through additional economic sanctions, as well as in ensuring Europe's defence and security," Tsahkna said. Estonia also supports reaching agreement on the EU's next long-term budget during Ireland's Presidency. Speaking about Ukraine, Tsahkna stressed that Europe must provide Ukraine with greater support and help the country move forward on its path towards accession to the European Union. "Ukraine's future lies in the European Union, and EU membership is the best long-term security guarantee for Ukraine," he said. The declaration of intent signed by Tsahkna and McEntee builds on existing Estonian-Irish development cooperation in Ukraine. Ireland's €1 million contribution to ESTDEV's 'Education and Healthcare for Ukraine' project will help improve rehabilitation and specialist medical care and train the specialists Ukraine needs. On increasing pressure on Russia, Tsahkna stressed the need to tighten sanctions and make progress on using frozen Russian assets for the benefit of Ukraine. "Russia must pay for the damage it has caused. Europe must respond more forcefully to the increasing attacks and subversive activities," he said. According to Tsahkna, the international isolation of Russia and Belarus must also continue, including in the fields of culture and sport, and access to the European Union for combatants who have fought in Russia's war must be restricted. "Aggression and war crimes must bring consequences," Tsahkna said. Estonia called on Ireland to take the next step and join the agreement establishing the Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression. Speaking about European security, Tsahkna noted that Russia's increasing attempts at sabotage and other subversive activities have not changed Estonia's threat assessment. "Russia poses a long-term threat to European security, and strengthening Europe's defence capabilities must remain our long-term priority," he said. According to Tsahkna, Estonia and Ireland are close partners with a similar understanding of the challenges facing Europe. "We have much in common, both in supporting Ukraine and in making Europe more secure," he said. The foreign ministers' joint press conference is available to watch online. Photos from the visit.

Photograph: Alaa Badarneh/EPA First Thing newsletter US news First Thing: Israel using US-made electroshock weapons on Palestinian detainees An American company is still supplying Taser weapons linked to abuse of prisoners by Israeli forces. Plus, 12 valuable lessons about life and death by hospice workers Martin Belam Thu 22 Oct 2026 06.48 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Good morning. An investigation has revealed that Israel is using US-made electroshock weapons on Palestinian detainees . American company Axon is still supplying the Taser weapons despite evidence they have been used to torture prisoners. The news comes as US volunteers including a lawmaker helping Palestinians harvest olives were detained, and Heidi Levine revealed more details of her violent assault by Israeli settlers. Human rights groups have condemned allegations of the repeated torture and ill-treatment of detainees held in Israeli detention centres and prisons using electric shock devices, with Amnesty calling for restrictions on exports of such devices. A spokesperson for the Israel Defense Forces said the abuse of detainees was strictly prohibited. Who was detained by Israel near Nahalin in the occupied West Bank? The Israeli military detained about 80 US, Israeli and British volunteers helping Palestinians harvest olives near Bethlehem, including the New York Democratic congressional nominee Brad Lander, several rabbis and Israel’s former deputy attorney general. Soldiers said the area had been declared a closed military zone. What more has Heidi Levine said about the Israeli settler attack on her? The Washington Post photojournalist who was attacked and seriously injured by Israeli settlers on Friday has described how she was saved with the help of local Palestinians . Witnesses said her beating only ceased when young men used slingshots to aim stones at the settlers, forcing them back. What is the latest development with US diplomats in the Middle E ast? The US state department has ordered some diplomats and the families of US government employees to leave Saudi Arabia , as it faces a barrage of near-daily attacks from Yemen’s Houthis. Reports have emerged of similar US withdrawals in UAE, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain amid concerns of a return to conflict with Iran after the midterm elections. State attorneys general step up plans to counter Trump’s meddling in midterms View image in fullscreen Donald Trump continues to make false charges of widespread voting fraud and veiled threats of interfering in the process. Photograph: Ümit Bektaş/Reuters Democratic state attorneys general, other top state officials and civic groups have accelerated planning to thwart any federal meddling in the November midterms by Donald Trump as he continues his false charges of widespread voting fraud and veiled threats of interfering in the process. The enhanced cooperation is significant because many secretaries of state are responsible for supervising elections, and state attorneys general are charged with defending the laws governing them. Where has Elon Musk been spending his election campaign money? Elon Musk’s Super Pac has spent more than $500,000 in New York’s highly competitive 17th congressional district race to help Mike Lawler, the Republican incumbent, hold his seat. Lawler, a moderate Republican, is fending off a challenge from Democrat Cait Conley in one of the most-watched races that could determine who controls Congress. What has happened with letters containing white powder being sent to Congress? Nancy Pelosi’s office received “a suspicious letter” on Wednesday in what appears to be the latest incident of ill-intentioned mailings targeted at US Congress members. The offices of more than three dozen members of Congress across the political spectrum have received envelopes containing white powder in recent days. What is Trump’s polling as the election looms? Donald Trump’s approval rating has sunk to 36% , the lowest recorded, with most respondents expressing frustration over his handling of the US economy, cost of living and Iran war. The president was heckled at least nine times during a campaign event yesterday, and reacted to a supporter punching a demonstrator by saying: “Man, I loved that.” Supreme court blocks Trump’s bid to restrict gender care for trans prisoners View image in fullscreen The decision marks an unusual victory for transgender rights before the nation’s highest court. Photograph: Kevin Lamarque/Reuters The US supreme court went against Donald Trump’s administration on Wednesday , refusing to allow the immediate enforcement of sweeping restrictions on gender-affirming care for transgender individuals held in prisons and federal facilities. The decision marks an unusual victory for transgender rights before the nation’s highest court, which has largely sided with the administration and other opponents of transgender rights in several major cases. Flaw in PHP computer language leads to shutdown of websites around world View image in fullscreen PHP is used by almost 70% of websites. Photograph: ANP/Shutterstock Websites around the globe have gone dark after a serious vulnerability was found in a computer language used to build much of the world wide web. Several European governments took down sites temporarily as they scrambled to patch the critical weakness in PHP, a language used by almost 70% of websites. The US National Security Agency told all organisations using PHP to take their systems offline if they were unable to patch them immediately. Our technology reporter Josh Taylor has this explainer on what PHP is, and how bad the flaw is. In other news … View image in fullscreen The French president, Emmanuel Macron. The US president blamed France’s violence on “migrants, jihadists and communists”. A 24-year-old Kansas man has been arrested for allegedly threatening to shoot Donald Trump .
